extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, petitioners, patent owners, and USPTO/Patent Trial & Appeal Board staff involved in post-grant and inter partes review proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules implementing AIA post-grant review (PGR) and inter partes review (IPR): who may file, timing, petition contents, institution standards, discovery and amendment procedures, estoppel, fees, and final decision/appeal mechanics before the PTAB/USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant review grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds for seeking post-grant review include any ground that could be raised under 35 U.S.C. 282(b)(2) or (3), except as modified by section 18(a)(1)(C) of the AIA; this includes grounds under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 (including prior art of patents or printed publications) and other grounds including 35 U.S.C. 101 and 112 (except best mode).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR is broader than IPR: PGR may raise 101 and 112 issues and other grounds under 282(b)(2)/(3) (except best mode). IPR grounds are limited to 102/103 and only on the basis of patents or printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a post-grant review (35 U.S.C. 321(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is not the owner of a patent may file a petition with the Office to institute a post-grant review of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director will establish by regulation fees to be paid by the requester in amounts reasonable considering aggregate costs of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: PGR timing limit (35 U.S.C. 321(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for post-grant review may only be filed not later than the date that is nine months after the date of the grant of the patent or the issuance of a reissue patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict statutory filing window for standard PGR petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PGR petition content requirements (35 U.S.C. 322(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition filed under 35 U.S.C. 321 may be considered only if it: (1) is accompanied by the fee; (2) identifies all real parties in interest; (3) identifies in writing and with particularity each claim challenged, the grounds for each challenge, and the evidence supporting each challenge (including copies of relied-upon patents/printed publications and affidavits/declarations if relying on other factual evidence or expert opinions); (4) provides other information the Director may require by regulation; and (5) provides copies of documents required under (2)-(4) to the patent owner or representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must give the Office and patent owner clear, particularized legal and factual bases and supporting exhibits for each challenged claim; failure to meet these elements bars consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of petition (35 U.S.C. 322(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as practicable after receipt of a petition under 35 U.S.C. 321, the Director will make the petition available to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions are generally public documents unless properly filed with an intent to seal and accompanied by a motion to seal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response right (35 U.S.C. 323)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PGR petition is filed, the patent owner has the right to file a preliminary response within a time period set by the Director, setting forth reasons why no PGR should be instituted based on failure to meet any statutory requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary responses attack procedural or threshold deficiencies; timing is set by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution standard for PGR (35 U.S.C. 324(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may not authorize a post-grant review to be instituted unless the Director determines that the information in the petition, if unrebutted, would demonstrate that it is more likely than not that at least one of the claims challenged is unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a 'more likely than not' threshold for institution, requiring the petition to present sufficient persuasive evidence on at least one claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative institution ground: novel or unsettled legal question (35 U.S.C. 324(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution determination may also be satisfied by showing that the petition raises a novel or unsettled legal question that is important to other patents or patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if the evidentiary threshold is marginal, a significant unsettled legal issue affecting other patents can justify institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institution decision timing and finality (35 U.S.C. 324(c),(d),(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will decide whether to institute a PGR within three months after receiving a preliminary response or, if none filed, the last date the response may be filed; the Director will notify parties and make notice public and include the review commencement date; the determination whether to institute is final and nonappealable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The institution decision is statutorily time-limited and not subject to appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preclusion based on prior civil action (35 U.S.C. 325(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A PGR may not be instituted if, before the date the petition is filed, the petitioner or real party-in-interest filed a civil action challenging the validity of a claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a civil action challenging validity before a PGR petition bars institution against that petitioner/real party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic stay and non-civil-action status of counterclaims (35 U.S.C. 325(a)(2)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A civil action brought by the petitioner or real party-in-interest challenging validity and filed on or after the PGR petition filing date may be automatically stayed until specified conditions are met; a counterclaim challenging validity does not constitute a civil action for these purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statute protects the interplay between PGRs and parallel district-court litigation, but counterclaims don't trigger the preclusion rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court consideration of preliminary injunction when civil action soon after grant (35 U.S.C. 325(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a civil action alleging infringement is filed within three months after grant, the court may not stay its consideration of the patent-owner's motion for a preliminary injunction on the basis that a PGR petition has been filed or instituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early-filed infringement suits retain the court's ability to rule on preliminary injunctions despite a PGR petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of multiple PGR petitions (35 U.S.C. 325(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: If more than one PGR petition is properly filed against the same patent and the Director determines more than one warrants institution, the Director may consolidate such reviews into a single PGR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation is discretionary to promote efficiency and avoid duplicative proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director authority to manage overlapping proceedings and repeated art (35 U.S.C. 325(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: During the pendency of a PGR, if another proceeding involving the patent is before the Office, the Director may determine how proceedings proceed (stay, transfer, consolidate, terminate); in deciding whether to institute or order proceedings, the Director may consider whether the same or substantially the same prior art or arguments were previously presented to the Office and may reject the petition on that basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director has broad procedural control and may deny redundant challenges to preserve administrative efficiency and finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel following final written decision in PGR (35 U.S.C. 325(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner (or real party-in-interest or privy) in a PGR that results in a final written decision may not request or maintain a proceeding before the Office with respect to that claim on any ground the petitioner raised or reasonably could have raised during that PGR; estoppel also applies in certain civil actions and ITC proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PGR final decisions create strong estoppel bar to relitigating grounds that were or could have been raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation re: reissue patents (35 U.S.C. 325(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A PGR may not be instituted if the petition requests cancellation of a claim in a reissue patent that is identical to or narrower than a claim in the original patent when the time limitations in 35 U.S.C. 321(c) would bar filing a petition for the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue substitutions cannot be used to evade the original PGR filing-time bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public file access and sealing (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will prescribe regulations making the file of any proceeding under chapter 32 available to the public, except that a petition or document filed with intent to be sealed will be treated as sealed pending ruling on the motion to seal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealing is possible but requires a motion; public access is the default.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations setting standards for sufficient grounds to institute (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director will prescribe regulations setting forth the standards for the showing of sufficient grounds to institute a review under 35 U.S.C. 324(a) and (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations will clarify evidentiary thresholds and standards applied at institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for supplemental information (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Director will establish procedures for submission of supplemental information after the petition is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules will govern when and how petitioners or parties may supplement the record post-filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery limited to directly related evidence (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations will establish standards and procedures for discovery of relevant evidence, including that discovery will be limited to evidence directly related to factual assertions advanced by either party in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discovery in PGRs/PTRs is narrower than in district court; focused on directly-related factual assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for abuse of discovery or process (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations will prescribe sanctions for abuse of discovery, abuse of process, or any other improper use of the proceeding, such as to harass or to cause unnecessary delay or an unnecessary increase in the cost of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may sanction parties who misuse the administrative process to harass or delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders for confidential information (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations will provide for protective orders governing the exchange and submission of confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties can seek protective orders to manage sensitive business-confidential materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner response after institution and evidence requirements (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations will provide for the filing by the patent owner of a response after a PGR is instituted, requiring that the patent owner file with such response, through affidavits or declarations, any additional factual evidence and expert opinions on which the patent owner relies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After institution, the patent owner may present testimonial evidence via affidavits/declarations; testimonial evidence is generally not permitted in preliminary responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend standards and public disclosure (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations will set forth standards and procedures for allowing the patent owner to move to amend the patent to cancel a challenged claim or propose a reasonable number of substitute claims, and ensure any information submitted in support of an amendment is made public as part of the prosecution history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendment requests are limited in scope, must not introduce new matter, and support materials become public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to oral hearing (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(10))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations will provide either party with the right to an oral hearing as part of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties will generally have at least one opportunity for oral argument before the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-year final determination timing and extension (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(11))
rubrics_metrics.description: The final determination in any PGR must be issued not later than one year after the Director notices the institution of a proceeding, except the Director may extend by not more than six months for good cause and may adjust time periods in cases of joinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory target is one year to final decision; extensions are limited and must be supported by good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner opportunity to file written comments (35 U.S.C. 326(a)(12))
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations will provide the petitioner with at least one opportunity to file written comments within a time period established by the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners have procedural opportunities to comment during the instituted proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for prescribing PGR regulations (35 U.S.C. 326(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: In prescribing regulations for PGR, the Director will consider effects on the economy, integrity of the patent system, efficient administration of the Office, and ability to complete timely proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory design must balance multiple public-interest and administrative objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB conducts post-grant reviews (35 U.S.C. 326(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Patent Trial and Appeal Board will conduct each post-grant review instituted under chapter 32 in accordance with 35 U.S.C. 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTAB is the adjudicatory body for PGRs under the AIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to amend: single motion and limits (35 U.S.C. 326(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: During a PGR the patent owner may file a single motion to amend to cancel any challenged claim and/or propose a reasonable number of substitute claims; additional motions may be permitted for settlement or for good cause; an amendment may not enlarge the scope of claims or introduce new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions to amend are tightly constrained: limited in number, cannot broaden claims, and may be allowed later only under specific circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof in PGR (35 U.S.C. 326(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: In a PGR instituted under chapter 32, the petitioner has the burden of proving a proposition of unpatentability by a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The evidentiary standard at PGR trial is preponderance of the evidence (lower than clear and convincing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination and settlement filing requirements (35 U.S.C. 327(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A PGR will be terminated with respect to any petitioner upon the joint request of the petitioner and patent owner (unless the Office already decided the merits); such a termination generally avoids estoppel for that petitioner; any settlement or understanding in connection with termination must be in writing and a true copy filed in the Office before termination, and may be treated as business confidential and kept separate from the patent file, available only to Federal agencies or to persons on showing good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement agreements must be filed; confidentiality may be preserved under specified conditions; termination by settlement affects estoppel differently than adjudicated termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written decision and certificate (35 U.S.C. 328(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PGR is instituted and not dismissed, the PTAB will issue a final written decision on patentability of challenged claims and any new claim added; after appeal time or termination of appeals, the Director will issue and publish a certificate canceling any claim finally determined unpatentable, confirming any claim determined patentable, and incorporating new or amended claims determined patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final decision and implementing certificate effect changes on the patent record, including cancellation or incorporation of amended claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of new or amended claims (35 U.S.C. 328(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposed amended or new claim determined patentable and incorporated into a patent following a PGR will have the same effect as specified in 35 U.S.C. 252 for reissued patents regarding rights of prior users, purchasers, or importers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful amended/new claims have statutorily defined retroactive/legal effects similar to reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reporting of PGR timing data (35 U.S.C. 328(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will make available to the public data describing the length of time between the institution of and the issuance of a final written decision for each PGR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timing metrics will be published to promote transparency and administrative accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights from PTAB PGR decisions (35 U.S.C. 329)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party dissatisfied with the PTAB final written decision may appeal pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 141-144; any party to the PGR will have the right to be a party to the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals follow statutory district-court/Federal Circuit pathways; parties to the administrative proceeding may participate in appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR is a trial subject to subpart A rules (37 C.F.R. § 42.100(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An inter partes review is a trial and subject to the rules set forth in subpart A of title 37, Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural and evidentiary trial rules apply to IPRs as specified in the CFR.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR claim construction standard: broadest reasonable interpretation (37 C.F.R. § 42.100(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim in an unexpired patent shall be given its broadest reasonable construction in light of the specification in which it appears.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office applies broadest reasonable interpretation (BRI) for claim construction in IPRs, consistent with historic PTO practice and justified by the opportunity to amend claims during IPR; cited precedents include Yamamoto and In re Am. Acad. of Sci.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR one-year administration timeframe (37 C.F.R. § 42.100(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a one-year time frame for administering the proceeding after institution, with up to a six-month extension for good cause; the one-year period may be adjusted by the Board in the case of joinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR proceedings have statutory timing targets similar to PGRs to promote prompt resolution; extensions are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file an IPR petition and filing bars (37 C.F.R. § 42.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party or real party-in-interest must file a petition prior to the filing of a civil action challenging the validity of a claim; a petition may not be filed more than one year after the date on which the petitioner or real party-in-interest was served with an infringement complaint; a petition may not be filed where the petitioner or real party-in-interest is estopped from challenging the claims on the grounds identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR petitions are barred by prior-filed civil actions, a one-year time bar after service of an infringement complaint, and estoppel from prior final decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR timeliness specifics (37 C.F.R. § 42.102)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for IPR must be filed consistent with 35 U.S.C. 311(c); petitions filed nine months after grant but prior to institution of a PGR are considered timely; petitions filed after termination of a PGR are timely; the Director may limit the number of IPRs instituted during each of the first four years but the Office did not expect to limit petitions at adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPR timing interacts with PGR windows; statutory cross-cutting time rules determine whether a petition is timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR fee and payment requirement (37 C.F.R. § 42.103)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee under § 42.15(a) must accompany a petition for IPR; no filing date will be accorded until full payment is received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full payment is required to obtain a filing date; fee payment is a jurisdictional prerequisite to petition consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR petition content: standing and particulars (37 C.F.R. § 42.104(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition must demonstrate standing: certify the patent is available for IPR and that the petitioner is not barred or estopped; the petition must identify each claim challenged, the specific grounds for each challenge, how claims are to be construed, why the claims as construed are unpatentable under the identified grounds, and exhibit numbers and citations to supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions must present precise, claim-by-claim legal/factual bases and exhibit citations; facially improper standing may be denied without reaching merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of clerical or typographical mistakes in IPR petitions (37 C.F.R. § 42.104(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner seeking to correct clerical or typographical mistakes in a petition may file a motion to correct; grant of such a motion does not alter the filing date of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerical fixes are possible by motion but do not change the statutory filing date or deadlines tied to the original filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR petition service requirements (37 C.F.R. § 42.105)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must serve the patent owner at the correspondence address of record and may serve any other address likely to effect service; upon agreement, service may be electronic, and service may be by EXPRESS MAIL® or means at least as fast and reliable; personal service is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service must follow specified channels to ensure patent owner notice; the correspondence address of record is primary.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPR filing date requirements and correction window (37 C.F.R. § 42.106)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition will not be accorded a filing date until it complies with § 42.104, is served on the patent owner at the correspondence address of record, and is accompanied by the fee; petitioners have one month to correct defective petitions after notice of incompleteness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board reviews procedural compliance and will notify petitioners of defects; a short cure period is available for certain defects but establishing a filing date requires satisfying all requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner preliminary response timing and content limits (37 C.F.R. § 42.107)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a preliminary response no later than three months from the notice that the petition has been granted a filing date; the Board has three months from filing of the preliminary response (or from its due date if none filed) to determine whether to institute; the preliminary response may not present new testimonial evidence (e.g., expert testimony), though in certain instances additional discovery before filing may allow submission of testimonial evidence obtained through discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary responses are for threshold arguments and may not include testimonial evidence; substantive testimonial evidence is reserved for post-institution responses through affidavits/declarations as permitted by statute.
